spa.name: Spa-Francorchamps
spa.unique: Legendary high-speed circuit with major elevation swings, forest microclimates, and one of the most famous corner sequences in motorsport.
spa.overview: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7.004 km challenge where commitment, aerodynamic balance, and confidence over crests decide lap time. It combines low-speed traction zones, very high-speed sweepers, and long full-throttle sections. Because the circuit runs through the Ardennes, weather can vary from one sector to another, which makes setup, tire management, and strategy unusually complex.
key_characteristics: Largest elevation profile in modern F1 calendar behavior.
Long lap amplifies every mistake; one small error can cost several corners.
Multiple overtaking windows through slipstream plus DRS.
Balance trade-off: low drag on straights versus confidence in fast corners.
strategy_focus: Rear stability through Eau Rouge-Raidillon influences the entire Kemmel run.
Brake temperature control is important after very long acceleration periods.
Variable weather means teams often hedge setup and pit timing windows.
Tire energy is high in high-speed corners like Pouhon and Blanchimont.
overtaking_hotspots: La Source after the start-finish straight.
Les Combes at the end of Kemmel DRS zone.
Bus Stop Chicane late-braking opportunity before the line.
historical_notes: Spa is widely regarded as one of the purest driver circuits in Formula 1.
The Eau Rouge-Raidillon complex is iconic for commitment and precision.
Frequent weather shifts have produced many strategy-defining races.

drs_zones.name: DRS Zone 1 (Kemmel)
drs_zones.detail: Activation after Raidillon, running uphill then flat toward Les Combes. This is the primary overtaking zone due to combined slipstream and DRS effect.

drs_zones.name: DRS Zone 2 (Start-Finish)
drs_zones.detail: Shorter second zone toward La Source. Better for pressure and setup moves than guaranteed passes.

sections.name: La Source
sections.significance: Tight hairpin that launches the lap downhill and is a primary attack point into the Ardennes run.
sections.cool_fact: Clean traction here matters because it dictates the entire approach to Eau Rouge.

sections.name: Eau Rouge
sections.significance: The first part of the legendary uphill compression sequence.
sections.cool_fact: The car compresses hard here before climbing immediately into Raidillon.

sections.name: Raidillon
sections.significance: Blind crest and commitment point that defines top speed onto Kemmel.
sections.cool_fact: A small lift here is visible in trap speed all the way to Les Combes.

sections.name: Kemmel Straight
sections.significance: The long uphill straight where drag level and slipstream effectiveness are exposed.
sections.cool_fact: This straight is one of the clearest demonstrations of aero efficiency in F1.

sections.name: Les Combes
sections.significance: Major braking zone after Kemmel and one of the best overtaking chances on the circuit.
sections.cool_fact: Late moves here often rely on the tow generated all the way from Raidillon.

sections.name: Malmedy
sections.significance: Fast transition corner where exit speed matters more than absolute apex aggression.
sections.cool_fact: A smooth steering trace here keeps the rear tires calmer for the middle sector.

sections.name: Speaker's Corner
sections.significance: A flowing right-hander that sets rhythm into the mid-circuit complex.
sections.cool_fact: This is one of the places where car balance differences are easy to spot visually.

sections.name: Bruxelles
sections.significance: Downhill braking corner requiring strong front-end bite and controlled rotation.
sections.cool_fact: It rewards drivers who can release the brakes smoothly without washing wide.

sections.name: Double Gauche
sections.significance: Long left-hand complex where mid-corner load and precision are critical.
sections.cool_fact: The long arc makes this one of the clearest aero-balance checks on the lap.

sections.name: Les Fagnes
sections.significance: Technical change-of-direction section that punishes rough curb usage.
sections.cool_fact: This area can separate a safe lap from an aggressive one very quickly.

sections.name: Campus
sections.significance: Exit-focused corner that leads toward the downhill return to Stavelot and the final sector.
sections.cool_fact: Drivers often sacrifice entry to guarantee traction on exit.

sections.name: Stavelot
sections.significance: Fast right-hander that starts the committed run back toward the final high-speed sector.
sections.cool_fact: Any early throttle allows a car to carry momentum into the next sector.

sections.name: Courbe Paul Frere
sections.significance: High-speed sweep that rewards bravery and smooth aerodynamic grip.
sections.cool_fact: This is one of the best places to see whether the car is planted over long load.

sections.name: Blanchimont
sections.significance: Extremely fast left-right area where total commitment is required.
sections.cool_fact: Tiny confidence differences here can separate the top of the field from the midfield.

sections.name: Chicane
sections.significance: Final braking and rotation zone before the finish line.
sections.cool_fact: The exit here is the last clean chance to defend into the timing line and Lap 1.

sections.name: Kemmel DRS
sections.significance: Primary DRS zone and major passing corridor.
sections.cool_fact: Combined DRS plus slipstream creates the biggest closing-speed delta on the lap.

sections.name: Start-Finish DRS
sections.significance: Secondary DRS zone that helps pressure the leader into Turn 1.
sections.cool_fact: This zone is more about setting up an overtake than always completing one.
